description:
Measured by the fz-kdt.199 research (2026-09-03, base ca23b676f) while
diagnosing why fz-kdt.120 cannot delete the fz-f98.16 empty-list cleaner.
THIS, not the activation key, is fz-kdt.120's real blocker.

THE DEFECT, read off activation dumps:

    key    List.reduce_cont/3[fp[L] list(int), fp[L] empty_list(), fp[va2] a2]
    return fp[T] {:done, empty_list()}      <-- WRONG; nothing here is collapsed
    key    List.reduce_cont/3[fp[L] list(int), fp[L] list(int), fp[va2] a2]
    return fp[T] {:done, list(int)}         <-- right

The first key names `empty_list()` at the accumulator because the caller seeded
`[]`, and that is CORRECT as a key -- nothing is collapsed and no two users
share it. The wrong part is the RETURN. `reduce_cont([a], b | c, ..) :: {:done,
b | c} | ..` instantiates `b|c := []` from the GROUND seed argument, and
refine_call_return then INTERSECTS that contract return with the observed one:
`[] <: list(int)`, so the meet is `[]` and the activation publishes `{:done,
[]}`. The list has been walked; the accumulator is no longer empty; the
published return says it is.

EVIDENCE IT IS THIS SEAM: disabling refine_call_return at ALL FIVE of its call
sites (semantic.rs:227, :1262, :1334, :1460, :1624/:1639; the fn at :1874) in a
throwaway diagnosis build makes the whole chain correct with the cleaner
deleted. Disabling any ONE site alone leaves the collapse -- no single site
owns it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PRECISION: the fz-f98.16 empty-list cleaner in
types/arrow_match.rs is currently the only thing discarding this stale binding.
fz-kdt.120 must delete that cleaner, and the moment it does, SEVEN corpus
fixtures produce WRONG ANSWERS (00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family,
enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs)
with Enum.map / to_list / with_index collapsing to []. Enum.reverse/1([int])
types as [].

THE SHAPE OF A FIX (not yet designed): a contract return variable instantiated
from a GROUND argument is evidence about that CALL, not a narrowing of the
activation's published return -- the accumulator's seed type is not the
accumulator's type after the walk. Either the instantiation must not bind a
return variable from a seed position the recursion overwrites, or
refine_call_return must not meet a contract return that was instantiated from a
non-invariant argument. fz-kdt.184's polarity split and fz-kdt.120's openness
axis both live in this calculator and neither is sufficient: openness cannot
open a GROUND witness, which is why fz-kdt.120's re-cut measured zero corpus
improvement over naive cleaner deletion.

NOT fz-kdt.199: that ticket keys a returned tuple FIELD and was measured
stacked -- with 199 applied and the cleaner deleted, all seven fixtures still
move and Enum.reverse/1([int]) still types as []. The wrong return sits on a key
with nothing collapsed, so no keying rule can reach it.

CONCORDANT: fz-kdt.190 (the same seam -- analyze_activation refining the
key-wide join by each row @spec result, and refine_observed_return keeping the
observed on an empty intersection -- but that ticket is about SOURCE-ORDER
dependence, a different defect at the same function); fz-kdt.184; fz-kdt.65
(closed; the join-only ladder that never re-narrows this).

RED-FIRST: reduce_cont keyed [list(int), empty_list(), a2] publishes {:done,
list(int)}; Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as [int]; and with the cleaner deleted
the seven fixtures stay correct on three doors.
title: A ground seed argument instantiates a @spec return variable and refine_call_return MEETS it into the published return: reduce_cont keyed on list(int) publishes {:done, []}
